It can fail if the shared harness converges to an average that underperforms a model-specific harness on the reader's actual production model, if the reader only uses one or two models (removing the diversity signal the method depends on), or if trajectory collection across API providers is rate-limited or expensive. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Forty Questions: Identifying a Language Model from One-Word Answers
item.description: The method replaces trusting provider labels or running heavyweight benchmark suites to verify which model an API endpoint actually serves, using a public census of default one-word answers and likelihood-based attribution. It costs cents per endpoint, requires no GPU, and adds only a small profiling script plus a reference answer database to the engineering stack. It can fail when a system prompt is injected (accuracy drops 6 to 16 points), when reasoning modes or provider-side context injection alter default answers, and it cannot resolve every endpoint, as two of 96 remained unidentified. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: ChartEvo: Self-Evolving Agent Harnesses for Long-Tail Chart Reasoning
item.description: It replaces manually engineered per-chart-type strategies and tools with a recursive framework that evolves reusable skills, executable tools, and tool-call chains driven by observed failures. It costs additional inference overhead from tool-augmented reasoning (partially controlled via learned local tool-call chains), plus the engineering complexity of maintaining an evolving skill and tool library around an API-based MLLM. It can fail if the self-improvement loop overfits to the evaluation distribution, if evolved tools are unreliable or unsafe to execute, and the reported gains are validated only on two chart benchmarks with a single proprietary base model. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration
item.description: Replaces ad hoc, empirically designed multi-agent collaboration protocols with a block-coordinate scheme in which agents propose local edits with cross-part corrections and a coordinator merges proposals only after checking them against a global objective. Costs include extra coordinator inference per round, correction-computation overhead, and implementation complexity, all multiplied by the number of API or model calls across agents. Can fail when local corrections are inaccurate (raising the error floor), when proposals frequently interfere and combination checks reject them, or on tasks without a decomposable global objective, where the protocol adds cost without convergence benefit. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Disclosure Begets Disclosure: A Self-Reinforcing Privacy Loop in LLM Agents with Persistent Memory
item.description: The technique replaces memory-write filtering and storage anonymization with a response-level instruction that prevents the agent from stating or presupposing stored personal attributes, breaking a self-reinforcing disclosure loop in persistent-memory agents. It costs only a system-prompt change and a small loss of personalization quality relative to full memory use, far less than the quality loss from filtering user input or stored content. It can fail if the instruction is not followed reliably across models or sessions, if inference-based leakage occurs without explicit presupposition, or if the simulated-user findings do not transfer to real user behavior. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
item.description: It replaces single-pass VLM spatial answering and specialized spatial-reasoning systems with an off-the-shelf general coding agent (e.g., Codex, Claude Code) wired to a command-line 3D perception toolkit, a persistent scene memory, and plain-language interpretation of tool readings. The cost is multi-turn agent-loop latency, increased token and API spend from iterative tool calls, and engineering effort to build and maintain the perception toolkit and memory layer, with no model training required. After adoption, gains can shrink as backbone models improve (the paper itself reports diminishing tool benefits), agent loops can misinterpret correct tool outputs or compound errors across steps, and results depend on the coverage and geometric accuracy of the perception tools in the target environment. 3 independent implementations, 144 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond the Point Mass: Acceptance-Derived Weights and Distributional Losses for Speculative Decoding
item.description: It replaces the point-mass cross-entropy drafter loss and D-PACE's position weights with overlap-derived (TV-based) acceptance weights and a Rényi-1/2 divergence loss during drafter training. It costs only a modification to the drafter training objective, roughly a 1.5% acceptance-length gain, and no inference-time changes, extra memory, or additional models. It can fail if the gains do not transfer beyond the Qwen3-4B setting tested, if the draft and target distributions are poorly matched so the divergence signal is noisy, or if a 1.5% acceptance improvement does not justify retraining an existing drafter pipeline. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FALCA: Falsification-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Deep Search Agents
item.description: Replaces single-agent iterative deep search with a propose-falsify loop in which independent Falsifier agents seek counterevidence and revise the research state, optionally reinforced by SFT warmup and RL with hierarchical credit assignment. The inference-time cost is roughly doubled LLM calls per step plus orchestration overhead, and the training component requires parallel rollouts and staged reward assignment that are expensive on a 24 GB GPU and likely only feasible via third-party APIs. The loop can fail if Falsifiers share the backbone's blind spots and rubber-stamp candidates, if falsification reports are noisy enough to destabilize the research state, or if hierarchical credit assignment misattributes rewards across stages. 3 independent implementations, 134 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design
item.description: OO-Harness replaces a single global agent harness (fixed prompts, tools, and control flow) with an evolved hierarchy of specialized harness subclasses selected per task by a router trained on execution records. The cost is an offline evolution phase in which an evolution agent runs tasks and generates/refines harness code, adding API spend and engineering complexity, though test-time routing itself is lightweight. It can fail when the router misclassifies tasks, when evolved harnesses overfit the training task distribution and generalize poorly to new task types, or when the evolution budget is too small to discover useful specializations. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies
item.description: RACE replaces full-dimensional per-head keys and queries (and reconstruction-based KV-cache compression) with a natively reduced-dimensional attention formed by selecting complete RoPE rotary pairs ranked by joint query-key activation energy, folding the selection into the model weights post-training. It costs a one-time calibration pass and permanently removes up to half of the head dimension, trading some representational capacity for lower KV-cache memory and attention FLOPs without custom kernels. It can fail if the calibration set is unrepresentative of production inputs, if accuracy on zero-shot or long-context tasks degrades at the chosen compression level, or if short-context workloads see little benefit since the gains concentrate at long contexts. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: VisualEvolve: A Skill Self-Evolution Framework for Visual Reasoning
item.description: Replaces reinforcement-learning fine-tuning of tool-use behavior with an external, evolving library of executable visual skills selected and refined through a Select-Execute-Evolve-Evaluate loop, with snapshot selection and progressive evidence access to control regressions. Cost is inference-time API or GPU compute for trajectory generation, skill evaluation on a held-out validation set, and engineering effort to maintain the skill library and evolution harness rather than model training. Failures include skill regressions propagating if snapshot selection is misconfigured, evolution driven by non-representative validation tasks, and accumulated API or compute spend when many evolution cycles are needed. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MAS-Guard: Unified Guardrails from Individual Agents to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
item.description: MAS-Guard replaces fragmented, single-threat defenses with a two-layer framework: per-agent task-specific guardrail experts (A-Guard) plus a system-level Control Plane enforcing developer-owned Agent Charters through deterministic route, capability, and message-format checks combined with semantic role and content assessment, with interventions of allow, reflection, confirmation, and block. It costs additional inference calls for the guardrail experts and semantic checks on agentic events, added latency per inter-agent message, and the engineering effort of authoring charters and deploying a control plane around existing agents. It can fail against opaque or compromised agents that bypass instrumentable layers, through semantic-check false positives that degrade benign-task utility, and against attack classes outside its six evaluation benchmarks. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: After the Attacker Leaves: Benchmarking Carryover Attacks on LLM Agents
item.description: This is an evaluation benchmark, not a deployable technique; it replaces single-session prompt-injection testing with multi-round measurement of memory-resident and scheduled-task payload re-firing. Running its 101 tasks against your agent costs API calls and engineering time, and the actionable finding is that defenses must sit at the runtime layer (memory-write gating, scheduled-task review) rather than in prompts. It can fail to transfer if your agent lacks persistent memory or heartbeat scheduling, and results on five frontier models may not predict behavior of the specific model and runtime you deploy. 4 independent implementations, 156 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Asymmetric Looped Transformers: Fixed Global Representations for an Iterative Decoder
item.description: It replaces full-stack layer looping, where one shared recurrent block both builds context and refines state, with a single-pass causal encoder producing fixed global KV caches plus a weight-tied recurrent decoder attending jointly to global and local KV. The cost is an architecture change requiring training from scratch, including a heavy-tail-guided layerwise learning-rate schedule, and some extra memory for per-layer global KV caches; there is no inference-time drop-in benefit. It can fail if the fixed-context/separate-refinement gains do not transfer beyond the FineWeb-Edu pretraining regime tested, and the absolute quality gain (~1.3 accuracy points) is modest relative to retraining cost. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.
